chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Muhammad ibn al-Salt, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) about a group of friends who were on a road, and the road was cut off to them (by bandits). So the thieves were seized, and some of them testified against others. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Their testimonies are not accepted except by the confession of the thieves themselves, or a testimony from others against them.'

key_terms.رِفْقَةٍ: a group or company of people

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for accepting testimony among thieves in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him), the principle of 'shahadat al-shuraka' (testimony of partners) is refined to address the specific context of thieves captured together. The Imam clarifies that while their mutual testimony is not automatically rejected, it is not sufficient on its own; it requires either a confession from the thieves themselves or independent testimony from other witnesses to be accepted. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the reliability and independence of witnesses, ensuring that the testimony of those with a shared interest or status (like thieves) does not stand alone without corroborating evidence.
